H01.description: Registers the new FR-GH-1 fence id in the guard-origin register, a consequence of the gh api fence fix.

H02.description: The executable-target regex omits workflow files, makefiles, justfiles, package manifests, Dockerfiles and CI/pre-commit configs, so a heredoc writing destructive content into them is classified non-executing and its body is not scanned.

H03.description: The segment command-word extractor does not skip shell reserved words (if/then/do/while...), so a body line like `if :; then rm -rf src; fi` yields `then` as the command word and the rm segment is dropped.

H04.description: Strips literal backticks from kept segments under a quoted delimiter so the new backtick normalisation does not create false positives; part of the backtick fix.

H05.description: Backtick command substitutions are never normalised, so no rule anchors on them and `echo "see `git push --force origin main`"` (or an unquoted heredoc body with backticks) passes the fence while its $( ) twin blocks.

H06.description: The scrub pipeline has no backtick-normalisation step before the rules run, letting backtick substitutions bypass every pattern.

H07.description: No rule refuses `gh api` with DELETE/PUT/PATCH (or GraphQL mutations) against refs, branch protection, tags, releases or the repository, so the REST escape hatch bypasses the force-push, branch-delete and spike fences.
